title: Counit-normalized exceptional scalar comparisons and common-stage descent
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, a field $k$ with $\ell$ invertible, and a complementary closed/open pair $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ with $X$ separated of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For every finite coefficient field $E\subset\Omega$, use the actual raw rational categories $D^b_c(T,E)$, and for $E\subset L$ their specified scalar functors $S_{T,L/E}=-\otimes_E L$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Suppose the exact functors $i_*,i^*,J_E,j^*,Rj_*$ give $i^*\dashv i_*\dashv J_E$ and $j^*\dashv Rj_*$, invertible closed/open counits, closed-to-open orthogonality in all shifts, and supported triangles with the actual adjunction maps. Assume the canonical coefficient comparisons for $i_*,i^*,j^*,Rj_*$ are invertible and normalized by derived tensor/pullback and the projection mate of the counit [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-direct-image].
Equip each right adjoint with the canonical shift structure induced by its specified adjunction and the fixed shift structure on its left adjoint [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique]. The canonical input coefficient comparisons are understood with their identity, scalar-associator and shift coherence, as specified in [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].
Then the scalar comparison for $Rj_*$ carries $S_{X,L/E}(\eta_{j,E})$ to $\eta_{j,L}$, and there is a unique natural isomorphism
$$b_{L/E}:S_{Z,L/E}J_E\xrightarrow{\sim}J_LS_{X,L/E}$$
whose closed pushforward preserves the exceptional counit. These $b$ are compatible with identity inclusions, successive inclusions, the actual scalar associators, exact shifts, and both adjunction maps. The supported triangles and all three arrows have these same compatibilities. The functors $J_E$ and their adjunctions therefore descend to the finite-field pair category $D^b_c(T,\Omega)$ with filtered-colimit Hom groups of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. The descended functor is right adjoint to the specified $i_*$; its supported triangles are distinguished, have the specified counit and open unit, and retain closed-to-open orthogonality. This assertion selects the mate-normalized maps and their coherent colimit action, rather than only a fieldwise family of isomorphic objects.

source.place: Algebraically closed stage: projection mate, scalar cocycle, shift compatibility and pair-category descent; returned step 12

proof.text: Write $I_E=i_{*,E}$, $Q_E=j_E^*$, $R_E=Rj_{*,E}$, and denote the exceptional counit by $e_E:I_EJ_E\to1$ and the open unit by $v_E:1\to R_EQ_E$. Suppress only the specified functor associators. Put $c:S_XI_E\xrightarrow{\sim}I_LS_Z$, $p:Q_LS_X\xrightarrow{\sim}S_UQ_E$, and $r:S_XR_E\xrightarrow{\sim}R_LS_U$. The assumption that $r$ is the counit projection mate means exactly that it is the right mate of $p$. The mate unit equation gives $r_{Q_EK}S_X(v_{E,K})=R_L(p_K)v_{L,S_XK}$. Consequently $t_K=R_L(p_K^{-1})r_{Q_EK}$ identifies $S_X(R_EQ_EK)$ with $R_LQ_LS_XK$ and satisfies $t_KS_X(v_{E,K})=v_{L,S_XK}$. This proves the claimed open-unit normalization; it is an equation of the actual maps.

source.place: Algebraically closed stage: normalize the open comparison by its projection mate; categories.tex Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints (unit form).

proof.text: The closed counit $i_E^*I_E\xrightarrow{\sim}1$ makes $I_E$ fully faithful: the adjunction bijection followed by this counit identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(I_EP,I_EQ)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(P,Q)$, with $I_E(f)$ corresponding to $f$. After scalar extension the given triangle for $K$ is distinguished. Its first vertex $A=S_XI_EJ_EK$ is identified by $c$ with $I_LS_ZJ_EK$, and its middle vertex is $M=S_XK$; step 1 identifies its last vertex $B$ with $R_LQ_LM$. Compare it with the specified $L$-triangle $A'=I_LJ_LM\xrightarrow{e_L}M\xrightarrow{v_L}B'$. Thus both last vertices are open and both first vertices are closed. All groups $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B'[n])$ vanish by the assumed closed-to-open orthogonality; the same applies with the two triangles interchanged. Scalar extension is exact by the canonical coefficient package in the hypotheses.

source.place: Algebraically closed stage: scalar extension of the supported triangle and closed full faithfulness.

proof.text: For these two triangles, postcomposition with $e_L:A'\to M$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(A,A')\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,M)$. Surjectivity follows from Hom-into-triangle exactness since $\operatorname{Hom}(A,B')=0$; injectivity follows by rotating the target triangle, since a map killed by $e_L$ factors through $B'[-1]$, whose Hom from $A$ is zero. Let $h:A\to A'$ be the unique lift of the scalar-extended first arrow $a:A\to M$. TR3 extends $(h,1_M)$ to $(h,1_M,u)$. Its last component is necessarily the previously specified $t:B\to B'$: the difference $u-t$ vanishes after the second arrow from $M$, hence factors through $A[1]$ by Hom-out-of-triangle exactness, and $\operatorname{Hom}(A[1],B')=0$. The last square therefore commutes. Since $1_M$ and $t$ are isomorphisms, $h$ is an isomorphism by the triangle-morphism two-out-of-three lemma. Full faithfulness of $I_L$ now lifts $hc^{-1}$ uniquely to $b_K:S_ZJ_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}J_LS_XK$. Its inverse lifts the inverse of $hc^{-1}$, so this is genuinely an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebraically closed stage: the orthogonal fibre comparison; derived.tex Tags 0149 (lemma-representable-homological) and 014A (lemma-third-isomorphism-triangle).

proof.text: The defining equation is $e_{L,S_XK}I_L(b_K)c_{J_EK}=S_X(e_{E,K})$. By the closed adjunction bijection this says exactly that $b$ is the mate of $c^{-1}:I_LS_Z\to S_XI_E$; the mate is a natural transformation and its counit equation is the displayed one. The bijection also shows that any counit-preserving natural transformation equals $b$. Its unit compatibility is the mate unit equation: $b_{I_EP}S_Z(\eta^J_{E,P})=J_L(c_P^{-1})\eta^J_{L,S_ZP}$. Thus both exceptional adjunction maps have the required coefficient normalization, not just the counit.

source.place: Algebraically closed stage: identify the exceptional comparison as the normalized right mate; categories.tex Tag 0B65.

proof.text:
For $E\subset L\subset N$, write $a_T:S_{T,N/L}S_{T,L/E}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{T,N/E}$ for the actual scalar associators. Pasting mates applied to the coherent inverse closed comparisons gives
$$b_{N/E}(a_ZJ_E)=(J_Na_X)(b_{N/L}S_{X,L/E})(S_{Z,N/L}b_{L/E}).$$
The identity square gives the identity mate, interpreted with the actual scalar unitors. Apply the same pasting identity to the squares for shift functors: the shift of $b$ and its value on a shifted object have the same counit transpose, since $c$ and scalar extension commute with shifts. The canonical right-adjoint shifts are the unique ones compatible with those left-adjoint shifts and counits, so these two comparisons agree. This proves identity, tower, associator and exact-shift coherence for $b$. No invertibility of a general right mate is being asserted: invertibility here was proved in step 3.

source.place: Algebraically closed stage: scalar cocycle and shift compatibility; canonical right-adjoint shifts and mate pasting.

proof.text: The preceding comparisons identify the first two arrows of each supported triangle, and step 3 proves that its third-arrow square also commutes. For completeness this comparison is unique among morphisms of these supported triangles extending a fixed middle map: the first component is forced by the injectivity of postcomposition with the target counit, and the last is forced by injectivity of precomposition with the source open unit, using the two Hom-exactness arguments in step 3. For two choices of a connecting arrow on the fixed three vertices, apply TR3 to the backward-rotated triangles and the identities on the middle and last vertices. The forced first component is the identity, so the last square says the two connecting arrows agree. Identities, composites, scalar towers and shifts therefore give the same maps on all three arrows; the finite-stage supported triangles are natural in $K$ for the same reason.

source.place: Algebraically closed stage: uniqueness of the triangle maps and compatibility of the connecting arrow; derived.tex Tags 0145 and 0149.

proof.text:
Apply coherent pair-functor descent to the additive exact families $J_E$ with comparisons $b$. It sends $(E,K)$ to $(E,J_EK)$. For a common-stage representative $u:S_{X,M/E}K\to S_{X,M/F}K'$, its value is
$$[M,b_{M/F,K'}^{-1}J_M(u)b_{M/E,K}].$$
The tower equation in step 5 is precisely the hypothesis making this independent of representatives and further fields. Apply the same descent to the already specified $i_*,i^*,j^*,Rj_*$ and to their compatible units and counits. The lemma descends compositions and equations, hence descends the two adjunction triangle identities. It also descends the three triangle arrows of step 6 as natural transformations. This uses the existing raw pair categories: no idempotents or new lattices are introduced.

source.place: Algebraically closed stage: functors and adjunction maps on common-field representatives.

proof.text: More explicitly, for $P=(E,P_E)$ on $Z$ and $K=(F,K_F)$ on $X$, identify the two common-stage Hom groups using the canonical comparisons for $I$ and $b$. At each $M\supset E,F$ the Hom bijection is $f\mapsto J_M(f)\eta^J_{M,S_{Z,M/E}P_E}$, with inverse $g\mapsto e_{M,S_{X,M/F}K_F}I_M(g)$. Their compatibility with enlarging $M$ is exactly the unit and counit equations of step 4. Thus both formulas pass to equivalence classes. Their composites are identities because at any common stage they are identities; their naturality for an arbitrary pair-category morphism is checked by representing that morphism and $f$ or $g$ at one common overfield. This gives natural inverse Hom bijections on the filtered-colimit Hom groups. The adjunction-of-bijections lemma identifies their unit and counit with the descended ones, since transposing the identity at its original finite stage gives those same maps.

source.place: Algebraically closed stage: actual adjunction Hom bijections on the filtered-colimit groups.

proof.text: Every pair-category object is $(E,K)$ and its supported triangle is the image of the $E$-triangle. The exactness of the finite-stage inclusion makes that image distinguished. Its first and second arrows are the specified descended exceptional counit and open unit by steps 6--8. Exactness of the descended $J$ can also be read directly: represent a distinguished triangle at a finite field $M$, apply the exact functor $J_M$, and use step 5 for its shift and step 7 for its arrows. Finally, for $P=(E,P_E)$, $N=(F,N_F)$, every element of $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*P[m],Rj_*N)$ is represented, after the operation and shift comparisons, in $\operatorname{Hom}(I_MS_{Z,M/E}P_E[m],R_MS_{U,M/F}N_F)$ for some $M\supset E,F$. This group is zero by the assumed finite-stage orthogonality. Every class is consequently zero, for every $m$.

source.place: Algebraically closed stage: distinguished triangles, exactness and cross-stage orthogonality.
